newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker in moderate trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker in moderate trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed softer on Friday at C$1.3492 (US$0.7412) from Thursday's close of C$1.3445 (US$0.7437) with most weakness stemming from overnight selling out of Switzerland, dealers said. * They said the weakness was part of a "healthy correction" after a sharp rally, but the long-term trend was to a stronger Canadian currency.
The Canadian dollar closed softer on Friday at C$1.3492 (US$0.7412) from Thursday's close of C$1.3445 (US$0.7437) with moderate trading volumes, dealers said.
"It's basically a bit more profit-taking and some of the funds liquidating some of their long positions," said one trader.
The currency lost most of its ground overnight on selling out of Switzerland which pushed the unit through a technical support level at C$1.3465 (US$0.7426), dealers said.
The currency drifted weaker for the rest of the day.

Some dealers said the recent weakness is part of a "healthy correction," but say the long-term trend to the currency is stronger. Others blamed the week's softer currency on some single large sell Canada orders.
"I don't think it's anything sinister," said one trader.
The currency rallied from C$1.3757 (US$0.7269) on January 2 to C$1.3366 (US$0.7482) on January 21, but has weakened steadily since then.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar eased to 1.2079 marks from Thursday's close of 1.2132 marks and slid to 88.11 yen from 88.71 yen.
